**Reference comparisons:**
- **Late Blight** (Bugwood_58): Field plants showing large dark brown irregular necrotic areas on leaves — somewhat similar pattern of extensive dark necrosis
- **Septoria** (CDDM_1035): Single leaf on grey background with scattered small spots — similar format and spot pattern to test image
- **Early Blight** (Bugwood_18): Field plants with brown/yellow leaf damage — less matching

- Most other references were microscopic or fruit/stem images not comparable to the leaf test image

**Decision:** The test image shows the combination of large irregular dark necrotic areas at leaf margins (characteristic of Late Blight) with small scattered darker spots in remaining green tissue. The large, irregular, dark-brown-to-black lesions predominantly at leaf margins/edges are most consistent with Late Blight (*Phytophthora infestans*), which causes water-soaked lesions that rapidly turn dark brown/black and can spread across the leaf.
